source_text: Concurrently, the Ugandan Rakai trial by Gray et al. involved 4,996 HIV-negative uncircumcised men aged 15–49, randomized to circumcision or control with 24-month follow-up ending September 2007.60313-4/fulltext) This yielded 67 HIV seroconversions (20 circumcised, 47 control), a 51% reduction in incidence (95% CI: 16–71%; adjusted HR 0.49, 95% CI: 0.29–0.82), again without increased risk behavior or sexual activity in the intervention group.60313-4/fulltext) Surgical complications were low (0.7% severe).60313-4/fulltext) The consistency across trials—each demonstrating approximately 50–60% efficacy against heterosexual HIV acquisition in high-prevalence sub-Saharan African settings—provided robust causal evidence from RCTs, surpassing prior ecological and observational associations.
